free_tier.stated: Up to 100 buckets, each up to 100 TB / 50 million objects; 5 TB max per object; regions FSN1/HEL1/NBG1

egress.terms: Base price includes 1 TB/month egress (1.1160 TB in a 31-day month, accumulated hourly). Overage verbatim: "Egress traffic: EUR 1.0000 per hour... per TB". Ingress, internal eu-central traffic, and all S3 API calls are free.

tooling: AWS CLI, rclone, all S3 SDKs
limits_note: Base price EUR 6.49/mo billed hourly at EUR 0.0104/h, charged for every hour a bucket exists even if empty. Storage overage EUR 0.0087 per TB-hour (= EUR 6.35/TB/month). Minimum billable object size 64 KB — pathological for small files.
reliability_note: LowEndTalk scepticism: "bandwidth limit is per bucket (not per object) and the pricing is based on 1TB increments it makes feel that it's just a fancy wrapped single-node storage with S3 compatibility, rather than actual distributed object storage".
confidence_note: The page states the number in the record; the claim is documented, not measured.

evidence.proved: the object storage page and its price row answer. Re-read https://www.hetzner.com/storage/object-storage/: HTTP 200, 7102 bytes, sha256 165549bb8b5db4ee.
